display.text:
@system_config = nil
      end

      def setup_global_logger(supervisor, supervisor_mode: false)
        cl_opt = supervisor.instance_variable_get(:@cl_opt) || {}
        opt = supervisor.class.default_options.merge(cl_opt)
        standalone_worker = opt[:standalone_worker]
        config_path = opt[:config_path]
        conf_encoding = opt[:conf_encoding]
        inline_config = opt[:inline_config]
        use_v1_config = opt[:use_v1_config]
        config_file_type = opt[:config_file_type]
        log_rotate_age = opt[:log_rotate_age]
        log_rotate_size = opt[:log_rotate_size]
        log_path = opt[:log_path]
        chuser = opt[:chuser]
        chgroup = opt[:chgroup]

        if supervisor_mode
          worker_id = 0
          process_type = :supervisor
        else
          worker_id = ENV['SERVERENGINE_WORKER_ID'].to_i
          process_type = case
                         when standalone_worker then :standalone
                         when worker_id == 0 then :worker0
                         else :workers
                         end
        end

        # Parse configuration immediately to initialize logger in early stage.
        # Since we can't confirm the log messages in this parsing process,
        # we must parse the config again after initializing logger.
        conf = Fluent::Config.build(
          config_path: config_path,
          encoding: conf_encoding,
          additional_config: inline_config,
          use_v1_config: use_v1_config,
          type: config_file_type,
        )
        system_sections = conf.elements(name: 'system')
        if system_sections.size > 1
          raise Fluent::ConfigError, "<system> is duplicated. <system> should be only one"
        end
        @system_config = supervisor.__send__(:build_system_config, conf)
        root_section = @system_config.instance_variable_get(:@config_root_section)
        params = root_section.to_h
        log_section = params[:log]
        log_level = @system_config.log_level
        dir_permission = params[:dir_permission]
        suppress_repeated_stacktrace = params[:suppress_repeated_stacktrace]
        ignore_repeated_log_interval = params[:ignore_repeated_log_interval]
        ignore_same_log_interval = params[:ignore_same_log_interval]

        # TODO: we should remove this logic. This merging process should be done
        # in `build_system_config()`.
        log_rotate_age ||= log_section.rotate_age
        log_rotate_size ||= log_section.rotate_size
        log_format = log_section.format
        log_time_format = log_section.time_format

        rotate = log_rotate_age || log_rotate_size
        actual_log_path = log_path

        # We need to prepare a unique path for each worker since Windows locks files.
        if Fluent.windows? && rotate && log_path && log_path != "-"
          actual_log_path = Fluent::Log.per_process_path(log_path, process_type, worker_id)
        end

        if actual_log_path && actual_log_path != "-"
          FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(actual_log_path)) unless File.exist?(actual_log_path)
          if rotate
            logdev = Fluent::LogDeviceIO.new(
              actual_log_path,
              shift_age: log_rotate_age,
              shift_size: log_rotate_size,
            )
            log_rotate_age = logdev.instance_variable_get(:@shift_age)
          else
            logdev = File.open(actual_log_path, "a")
          end

          if chuser || chgroup
            chuid = chuser ? ServerEngine::Privilege.get_etc_passwd(chuser).uid : nil
            chgid = chgroup ? ServerEngine::Privilege.get_etc_group(chgroup).gid : nil
            File.chown(chuid, chgid, actual_log_path)
          end

          if dir_permission
            File.chmod(dir_permission || Fluent::DEFAULT_DIR_PERMISSION, File.dirname(actual_log_path))
          end
        else
          logdev = STDOUT
        end

        $log = Fluent::Log.new(
          # log_level: subtract 1 to match serverengine daemon logger side logging severity.
          ServerEngine::DaemonLogger.new(logdev, log_level: log_level - 1),
          path: actual_log_path,
          process_type: process_type,
          worker_id: worker_id,
          format: log_format,
          time_format: log_time_format,
          suppress_repeated_stacktrace: suppress_repeated_stacktrace,
          ignore_repeated_log_interval: ignore_repeated_log_interval,
          ignore_same_log_interval: ignore_same_log_interval,
        )
        $log.enable_color(false) if actual_log_path
        $log.enable_debug if $log.level <= Fluent::Log::LEVEL_DEBUG

        $log.info "init #{process_type} logger",
                  path: actual_log_path,
                  rotate_age: log_rotate_age,
                  rotate_size: log_rotate_size
      end
    end

part.text:
Fixed. The issue was in lib/fluent/system_config.rb:66 — `rotate_age` parsed the enum value `"daily"` into a symbol (`:daily`), but Ruby's `Logger::Period#next_rotate_time` only accepts strings (`"daily"`, `"weekly"`, `"monthly"`), causing the `ArgumentError` from `logger/period.rb:21`.

Changed `v.to_sym` to `v` so the value stays a string (integers still parse via `Integer(v)`).

Verified:
- `test/config/test_system_config.rb`: 29 tests, 100% passed
- `test/test_supervisor.rb`: 43 tests, 100% passed
- `test/test_log.rb`: 108 tests, 100% passed
- `test/test_config.rb` has one pre-existing failure (`test_include`, also fails with the change stashed — environment-related, unrelated to this fix)
- End-to-end check: `Fluent::SystemConfig` now returns `"daily"` and `Fluent::LogDeviceIO` accepts it for daily rotation
